performed_via_github_app.description:
Codecov provides highly integrated tools to group, merge, archive and compare coverage reports. Whether your team is comparing changes in a pull request or reviewing a single commit, Codecov will improve the code review workflow and quality.

## Code coverage done right.®

1. Upload coverage reports from your CI builds.
2. Codecov merges all builds and languages into one beautiful coherent report.
3. Get commit statuses, pull request comments and coverage overlay via our browser extension.

When Codecov merges your uploads it keeps track of the CI provider (inc. build details) and user specified context, e.g. `#unittest` ~ `#smoketest` or `#oldcode` ~ `#newcode`. You can track the `#unittest` coverage independently of other groups. [Learn more here](
http://docs.codecov.io/docs/flags)

Through **Codecov's Browser Extension** reports overlay directly in GitHub UI to assist in code review in [Chrome](https://chrome.google.com/webstore/detail/codecov/gedikamndpbemklijjkncpnolildpbgo) or Firefox (https://addons.mozilla.org/en-US/firefox/addon/codecov/)

*Highly detailed* **pull request comments** and *customizable* **commit statuses** will improve your team's workflow and code coverage incrementally.

**File backed configuration** all through the `codecov.yml`. 

## FAQ
- Do you **merge multiple uploads** to the same commit? **Yes**
- Do you **support multiple languages** in the same project? **Yes**
- Can you **group coverage reports** by project and/or test type? **Yes**
- How does **pricing** work? Only paid users can view reports and post statuses/comments.

body: Awesome! Stoked to stop doing OptInt and OptString in slides. I haven't reviewed the code yet, just been trying it out on the slides. The one thing I'm having to fix in the B2T2 slides is constructors in synthetic position. Example from one of the B2T2 slides: Need to add an explicit Some@(...) TypAp or an : Option(T) ascription. Should we open a GitHub issue to track implicit application in synthetic position after this is merged?

From a user perspective I think the distinction between `typfun`, which introduces a _higher kinded_ type vs. `poly`, which is a (possibly higher rank) _polymorphic_ type, is a bit difficult to notice. Both of these do different things, but look/sound annoyingly similar. Distinction: - Higher kinded types can be applied at the type level, and must be fully applied. - A polymorphic type is a singleton kind `Type`, cannot be applied at the type level, but its values can be partially applied at the value level (`_@`) Yet writing `type Id = typfun A -> (A -> A)` vs `type Id = poly A -> (A -> A)` look quite similar. I feel it makes sense to entirely disallow writing `typfun` explicitly to make this a little more obvious. Especially given the `explainThis` doesn't say anything about how `typfun` construct works. Anyway, here's a little example we could use as a base for some docs for demonstrating the difference: (ok technically these are order 1 kinded types, not higher kinds, but you get what I mean)

Also, allowing writing `typfun` allows some very weird annotations which should definitely be erroneous, but aren't caught. Despite higher kinds not being allowed in annotations, I can literally annotate a value with a higher kind directly (`typfun`). Both uses below should error: I think it makes sense to entirely disallow writing `typfun` in the surface syntax. Is there any genuine use for it? Since it doesn't make sense to write type aliases containing higher kinded types not in prenex normal form. (Technically our current function def syntax doesn't allow things like `type Either(A)(B) = ...` for curried types, or `let f(a)(b) = ...` for curried functions, so you would probably need to add this synrax.)

Here is the relevant scratch file (.txt so github can upload)
[poly_vs_typfun.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30467066/poly_vs_typfun.txt)
Also, reminder to add an ExplainThis entry for `typfun`
There is also an issue with constructor resolution for curried typfuns: (D is not found)
